TINY (1-3% of frame) — the anchor entity is a SILHOUETTE-SIZED witness occupying ~2% of the frame, placed at MIDGROUND-BACK or DEEP-MIDDLE position. The world is the hero; the entity proves the world is impossibly large. Render the entity small enough that face detail is invisible — pose is via silhouette alone.

SMALL (5-10% of frame) — the anchor entity is at MIDGROUND distance, occupying ~5-10% of the frame. Recognizable as a figure or craft but not yet a portrait. The eye still finds the entity first, but the surrounding environment fills the remaining 90%.

MEDIUM (15-25% of frame) — the anchor entity is the visual protagonist, at midground-forward distance, occupying 15-25% of the frame. Face and pose detail visible but environment still wraps around. Character moment in a setting.

LARGE (30-40% of frame) — the anchor entity is portrait-scale, foreground-positioned, occupying 30-40% of the frame. Environment is backdrop, not co-star. The entity's expression and detail carry the story.
